Un prototype authentifié, porté sur une course sur route aux États-Unis il y a quelques jours. Et clairement, Nike ne fait plus dans la demi-mesure. 🧵👇 ↩️ Un virage à 180° Avec les Vaporfly 3 et 4, Nike avait fait le choix d’un design plus accessible, une géométrie de semelle plus plate, plus stable, plus grand public. Là, la marque fait exactement le chemin inverse : une semelle ultra-agressive qu’on n’avait jamais vue chez le Swoosh. 👀 Ça vous rappelle quelque chose ? Forcément. Cette géométrie fait immédiatement penser à la Puma Fast-R 3 — la paire avec laquelle Yann Schrub a pulvérisé le record d’Europe du 10km cet hiver, et qui fait quasiment l’unanimité chez les élites en ce moment. Nike semble avoir pris note. 📅 Et la suite ? La Vaporfly 4 étant sortie l’année dernière, ces prototypes laissent imaginer une sortie au printemps 2027 — vraisemblablement après l’Alphafly 5 et le mystérieux projet APEX, la nouvelle hyper-chaussure Nike dont on vous a déjà parlé. A spoonful of chili oil and seafood make everything hotter and better.🔥 Shrimp heads, soft tofu, crab, octopus, and juicy shrimp simmer into a rich, spicy broth that’s guaranteed to bring you back to life❤️‍🔥 Would you try this after a night out?🍜✨ 📍 Tag your late-night buddy & save this recipe for your next rough morning ✨ Hailey’s Hangover Seafood Tofu Ramen 📝 Ingredients * 2–3 tbsp chili oil * 2 eggs * 1 green onion, chopped * 2–3 cloves garlic, sliced * 1 pack Shin Ramyun (soup base + veggie packet) * 2 cups water * 3–5 large shrimp (heads separated) * 1 small crab * Baby octopus * Soft tofu * Rice cakes * A handful of bok choy (or bean sprouts) * Fresh red chili, sliced 👩‍🍳 Instructions 1. Heat the chili oil over medium heat. Crack in one egg and let the edges crisp slightly. 2. Add the shrimp heads, crab, baby octopus, garlic, and green onion. Sauté for about 1 minute until fragrant. 3. Remove the egg and octopus so they don’t overcook. 4. Stir in the Shin Ramyun soup base and veggie packet, then pour in the water. Bring to a boil. 5. Add the noodles, soft tofu, rice cakes, and shrimp. Cover and cook for about 2 minutes. 6. Return the octopus and add the bok choy. Cook just until the shrimp turn pink and the bok choy is tender-crisp. 7. Top with the crispy egg, an extra egg yolk (optional), and fresh red chili. Enjoy immediately. 💡 Tip: Add a splash of soy sauce if the broth needs a little more seasoning.  #asmrfood #mukbang #ramenhacks #hangovercure #fyp

top 5 tips to start your healthy hair care journey🌱✨ 1. cut off those split ends✂️      split ends can’t be repaired, only temporarily sealed. if you leave them, they can continue splitting farther up the hair shaft, leading to more breakage over time. regular trims help keep your hair looking thicker and healthier while preventing you from losing more length later. 2. do a 10 minute scalp massage daily💆🏼‍♀️      your scalp is skin, and healthy hair starts there. daily scalp massages can help increase blood flow to the scalp, reduce buildup, and create a healthier environment for your hair to grow. you can use your fingertips or a scalp massager. just be gentle and consistent. 3. start scalp + hair oiling🫶      find the right hair oil for your scalp and hair type because not every oil works for everyone. i oil my scalp for density, not to make my hair grow faster. massage it in for a few minutes 1 to 3 times a week before wash day, then wash it out after 3 to 4 hours if your scalp tolerates it well. i also have other videos that go into all the do’s and don’ts of hair oiling if you want to learn more. 4. get a blood panel done🩸      if your hair feels thinner than normal, sheds excessively, or isn’t growing like it used to, it may be worth asking your doctor for blood work. things like low iron, vitamin d, b12, zinc, or other deficiencies can affect hair health. if you’re deficient, focus on vitamin rich foods and only take supplements if recommended by your healthcare provider. 5. learn your hair before buying products🤍      figure out your hair pattern (straight, wavy, curly, or coily), strand texture (fine, medium, or coarse), porosity (how well your hair absorbs and holds moisture), and scalp type (oily, dry, balanced, or sensitive). once you know those, it’s much easier to build a routine that actually works for you instead of wasting money on products that aren’t a good fit. healthy hair isn’t about buying the most expensive products. it’s about understanding your hair, staying consistent, and being patient. 🤍   #haircare #healthyhair #HairCareTips #kayliboyle
